goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 stores feed content as raw HTML without sanitization, enabling persistent JavaScript injection in topic/embed viewers

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: In topic_embed.rb, the `import` method takes `contents` and passes it to `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb, when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, the `cook` method returns `raw` directly without any sanitization. The content from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb) uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` which doesn't sanitize HTML. The content from remote URLs (import_remote) uses ruby-readability which extracts content but doesn't sanitize for XSS. In the embed view (best.html.erb), the content is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` which outputs unescaped HTML. This creates a clear XSS vulnerability path: malicious content in RSS feeds or embedded URLs can contain JavaScript that will be executed when viewing the topic or embed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 follows user-influenced URLs and redirects without revalidating destinations or blocking private/link-local addresses, enabling SSRF via redirects or DNS rebinding

adjudication.rationale: Looking at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48, the code uses `open(url).read` where `url` comes from user input (the embed_url parameter). The `open` method from Kernel (or open-uri) will follow HTTP redirects automatically. There's no validation that the URL points to a safe destination - it could be redirected to internal/private IP addresses (127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 169.254.x.x, etc.) or file:// URLs. This is a classic SSRF vulnerability. The code at line 48 is: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. The URL comes from `import_remote(user, url, opts=nil)` which is called from `fetch_http` in topic_retriever.rb and from poll_feed.rb. While there's a check that `embed_url` matches `embeddable_host` in topic_retriever.rb, this doesn't prevent DNS rebinding attacks or redirect-based SSRF. The finding correctly identifies a real SSRF vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 calls downcase on a blank SiteSetting.embed_by_username value, causing new embeds to remain on the loading page

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lib/topic_retriever.rb:49, the code is `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`. If `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is blank/nil, calling `.downcase` on it would raise a NoMethodError. However, examining the code flow: `fetch_http` is only called from `perform_retrieve`, which is only called from `retrieve` when `!invalid_host? && !retrieved_recently?`. The `invalid_host?` check requires `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` to match the URL host. Looking at the broader context, in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:16-17`, there's a guard `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` before calling `poll_feed`. However, in `topic_retriever.rb`, there's no such guard before calling `fetch_http`. If `embeddable_host` is set but `embed_by_username` is blank, and a user triggers the embed flow, `fetch_http` would be called and `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` would fail on a blank string. Actually, calling `.downcase` on an empty string '' returns '', which is valid. But if it's `nil`, it would raise an error. Looking at site_settings.yml, `embed_by_username: ''` is the default, so it would be an empty string, not nil. Calling `''.downcase` returns `''`, which is valid. The User.where query would just return no results, and `user.blank?` would be true, causing an early return. So this is not actually a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 defines embed_url as a default-length string, causing valid URLs longer than 255 characters to fail during embed insertion after partial processing

adjudication.rationale: The migration at db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb defines embed_url as 't.string :embed_url, null: false' without specifying a length limit. In Rails/ActiveRecord, a string column without an explicit limit defaults to 255 characters in most databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL). URLs can legitimately exceed 255 characters, especially with query parameters. The code in TopicEmbed.import and other places stores URLs in this column. If a URL longer than 255 characters is provided, the database insert would fail. This is a real potential bug - the schema design could cause data truncation or insertion failures for valid long URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39 expects TopicRetriever to be instantiated and invoked, but the controller now calls Jobs.enqueue, so the test cannot pass

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb line 14-15, when topic_id is nil, the controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, in the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:39-43, the test expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`. This is a mismatch - the controller enqueues a job, but the test expects direct TopicRetriever instantiation. The test would fail because TopicRetriever.new is never called directly by the controller; instead Jobs.enqueue is called. The actual TopicRetriever is called inside the job (lib/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), not in the controller. This is a real test failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:21 never uses feed_key, causing the hourly job to download and parse the entire feed instead of using modification caching

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, I can see that `feed_key` method is defined (lines 20-22) but never called anywhere in the class. The method creates a Redis key based on the feed URL hash, which appears intended for caching/modification tracking. However, the `poll_feed` method simply downloads and parses the feed every time without checking or using this key. This is a real issue - the code defines infrastructure for caching but doesn't use it, meaning the hourly job will always re-download and re-process the entire feed unnecessarily.
